hook: One meal carried Elijah for forty days.

verse.translation: He arose, and ate and drank, and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights to Horeb, God’s Mountain.

story: Running for his life, the prophet Elijah lay down under a juniper tree in the wilderness and asked God to take his life.

An angel woke him with bread and water: “Arise and eat, because the journey is too great for you.” On the strength of that food he walked forty days and forty nights to Horeb, where God spoke to him in a still small voice.
The church names Elijah with Moses as the prophets whose forty-day fasts this one remembers. Centuries later, the two of them appeared beside Jesus at the Transfiguration.
meaning: Elijah couldn't finish the road on his own strength; God fed him for it. The fast asks the same of us: lean on God for the strength to finish.

sources.title: 1 Kings 19:4–12 and Matthew 17:3, World English Bible (public domain)
